items.title: 10.3 Further Application of Basic Identities (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Assalam o alaikum! Pichle sabaq (10.1.2) mein humne sum aur difference ke formulas prove kiye the, aur 10.2 mein allied angles ke rules seekhe the. Ab waqt hai un formulas ko kaam mein lane ka. Is hisse mein kitab koi lambi theory nahin deti; seedha chhe (6) solved examples deti hai. Har example ek naya tareeqa sikhata hai: kabhi identity prove karna, kabhi aisa angle jo table mein nahin (jaise \(105^{\circ}\)), kabhi quadrant dekh kar sign chunna, kabhi triangle ke angles, aur aakhir mein ek expression ko \(r\sin(\theta + \phi)\) ki shakal mein likhna. Aap har example ko dhyan se dekhiye ke kaunsa formula kyun chuna gaya.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh formulas is poore sabaq ki bunyaad hain, inhein zabani yaad hona chahiye:
\[\sin(\alpha \pm \beta) = \sin\alpha\cos\beta \pm \cos\alpha\sin\beta\]
\[\cos(\alpha \pm \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta \mp \sin\alpha\sin\beta\]
\[\tan(\alpha \pm \beta) = \dfrac{\tan\alpha \pm \tan\beta}{1 \mp \tan\alpha\tan\beta}\]
\[\sin^{2}\theta + \cos^{2}\theta = 1\]
\(\pm\) aur \(\mp\) ko aise parhiye: upar wale signs ek saath, neeche wale signs ek saath. Cosine wale formula mein ek khaas baat hai: angle mein plus ho to beech mein minus aata hai, aur angle mein minus ho to beech mein plus. Yeh ulta sign bohat se students bhool jate hain, is liye shuru se hi is par nazar rakhiye.
Aakhri wali identity \(\sin^{2}\theta + \cos^{2}\theta = 1\) (Pythagorean identity) har jagah kaam aati hai: jab ek ratio diya ho aur doosra chahiye ho, ya jab cos ko sin mein badalna ho.

blocks.title: Example 5
steps:
Given: product \(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\sin(\alpha - \beta)\).
To prove: yeh \(\sin^{2}\alpha - \sin^{2}\beta\) (i) ke barabar hai, aur \(\cos^{2}\beta - \cos^{2}\alpha\) (ii) ke barabar bhi.
Method: sab se pehle dekhte hain ke kis side se shuru karein. Hamesha us side se shuru kariye jo zyada 'bhari' (complicated) ho; yahan L.H.S. mein brackets hain jo khul sakti hain. Plan: dono factors ko sum aur difference formula se kholein, multiply karein, phir \(\cos^{2}\) ko \(1 - \sin^{2}\) mein badlein taa ke sirf sines bachein.

Step 1: Dono factors kholein
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \sin(\alpha + \beta)\sin(\alpha - \beta)\]
\[= (\sin\alpha\cos\beta + \cos\alpha\sin\beta)\]
\[\times(\sin\alpha\cos\beta - \cos\alpha\sin\beta)\]
Kyun: \(\sin(\alpha \pm \beta) = \sin\alpha\cos\beta \pm \cos\alpha\sin\beta\). Ghor kariye, dono brackets bilkul ek jaisi hain, sirf beech ka sign alag hai. Yeh ishara hai ke aage koi aasan algebraic identity lagegi.

Step 2: \((x + y)(x - y) = x^{2} - y^{2}\) lagayein
\[= \sin^{2}\alpha\cos^{2}\beta - \cos^{2}\alpha\sin^{2}\beta\]
Kyun: \(x = \sin\alpha\cos\beta\) aur \(y = \cos\alpha\sin\beta\) maan lein to yeh seedha difference of squares hai. Chaar terms ki lambi multiplication ki zaroorat nahin; beech wale cross terms khud hi cancel ho jate hain.

Step 3: Cosines ko sines mein badlein
\[= \sin^{2}\alpha(1 - \sin^{2}\beta) - (1 - \sin^{2}\alpha)\sin^{2}\beta\]
\[= \sin^{2}\alpha - \sin^{2}\alpha\sin^{2}\beta\]
\[\quad - \sin^{2}\beta + \sin^{2}\alpha\sin^{2}\beta\]
\[= \sin^{2}\alpha - \sin^{2}\beta \quad \text{(i)}\]
Kyun: humari manzil (i) mein sirf sines hain, is liye har \(\cos^{2}\) ko \(1 - \sin^{2}\) se badal diya. Ab \(-\sin^{2}\alpha\sin^{2}\beta\) aur \(+\sin^{2}\alpha\sin^{2}\beta\) aapas mein cancel ho gaye.
Dhyan dein: \(-(1 - \sin^{2}\alpha)\sin^{2}\beta\) kholte waqt minus dono terms par lagta hai: \(-\sin^{2}\beta + \sin^{2}\alpha\sin^{2}\beta\).

Step 4: Result (i) ko cosines mein badlein
\[= (1 - \cos^{2}\alpha) - (1 - \cos^{2}\beta)\]
\[= 1 - \cos^{2}\alpha - 1 + \cos^{2}\beta\]
\[= \cos^{2}\beta - \cos^{2}\alpha \quad \text{(ii)}\]
Kyun: ab ulta kaam: \(\sin^{2}\theta = 1 - \cos^{2}\theta\). Dono 1 cancel ho gaye. Order par ghor kariye: (ii) mein \(\cos^{2}\beta\) pehle hai, \(\cos^{2}\alpha\) baad mein. Yahan order ulat jata hai, kyun ke minus ki wajah se signs badal gaye.

Tasdeeq:
Ab ek aasan angle rakh kar dekhte hain: \(\alpha = 60^{\circ}\), \(\beta = 30^{\circ}\). L.H.S. \(= \sin 90^{\circ}\sin 30^{\circ} = 1\times\frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{2}\).
(i): \(\sin^{2}60^{\circ} - \sin^{2}30^{\circ} = \frac{3}{4} - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{1}{2}\).
(ii): \(\cos^{2}30^{\circ} - \cos^{2}60^{\circ} = \frac{3}{4} - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{1}{2}\). Teeno barabar, is liye proof sahi hai. (Yaad rahe, ek misaal proof nahin hoti, sirf tasdeeq hoti hai.)

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Is natije ko ek tayyar identity ki tarah yaad kar lijiye: \(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\sin(\alpha - \beta) = \sin^{2}\alpha - \sin^{2}\beta\). Board ke paper mein aksar aise sawal aate hain jahan yeh seedha kaam aata hai. Isi tarah ke steps se iska saathi natija \(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\cos(\alpha - \beta) = \cos^{2}\alpha - \sin^{2}\beta\) bhi nikalta hai; ise khud practice ke liye prove kariye.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Agar \(\alpha = \beta\) ho to Example 5 ka L.H.S. kya ban jata hai? \(\sin 2\alpha \cdot \sin 0 = 0\). Aur R.H.S. \(\sin^{2}\alpha - \sin^{2}\alpha = 0\). Dono zero, yani natija is khaas soorat mein bhi sahi baith raha hai.
Ab agla example ek bohat kaam ka tareeqa sikhata hai: aisa angle jis ki value table mein yaad nahin, use do jaane pehchaane angles ke jor se likh do.

blocks.title: Example 6
blocks.problem: Without using tables, find the values of all trigonometric functions of \(105^{\circ}\).
steps:
Given: angle \(105^{\circ}\), jo special angles (\(0^{\circ}, 30^{\circ}, 45^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}, 90^{\circ}\)) mein nahin aata.
To find: \(105^{\circ}\) ke chhe ke chhe trigonometric functions: \(\sin\), \(\cos\), \(\tan\), \(\cot\), \(\operatorname{cosec}\), \(\sec\).
Method: \(105^{\circ} = 60^{\circ} + 45^{\circ}\) likhein. Dono angles ki exact values humein yaad hain, is liye sum formulas laga kar \(\sin\), \(\cos\), \(\tan\) nikalenge. Baqi teen sirf ulte (reciprocal) hain, unke liye fraction ko ulat dena kaafi hai.

Step 1: \(\sin 105^{\circ}\)
\[\sin 105^{\circ} = \sin(60^{\circ} + 45^{\circ})\]
\[= \sin 60^{\circ}\cos 45^{\circ} + \cos 60^{\circ}\sin 45^{\circ}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2\sqrt{2}}\]
Kyun: \(\sin(\alpha + \beta) = \sin\alpha\cos\beta + \cos\alpha\sin\beta\). Values: \(\sin 60^{\circ} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), \(\cos 60^{\circ} = \frac{1}{2}\), \(\sin 45^{\circ} = \cos 45^{\circ} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\). Dono fractions ka denominator \(2\sqrt{2}\) same hai, is liye numerators jama ho gaye.

Step 2: \(\cos 105^{\circ}\)
\[\cos 105^{\circ} = \cos(60^{\circ} + 45^{\circ})\]
\[= \cos 60^{\circ}\cos 45^{\circ} - \sin 60^{\circ}\sin 45^{\circ}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1-\sqrt{3}}{2\sqrt{2}}\]
Kyun: \(\cos(\alpha + \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta - \sin\alpha\sin\beta\) (beech mein minus!). Jawab negative hai kyun ke \(\sqrt{3} \approx 1.73\) se \(1 - \sqrt{3}\) manfi hai. Yeh theek bhi hai: \(105^{\circ}\) doosre quadrant mein hai jahan cosine negative hota hai.

Step 3: \(\tan 105^{\circ}\)
\[\tan 105^{\circ} = \dfrac{\tan 60^{\circ} + \tan 45^{\circ}}{1 - \tan 60^{\circ}\tan 45^{\circ}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{3}+1}{1-\sqrt{3}\cdot 1} = \dfrac{1+\sqrt{3}}{1-\sqrt{3}}\]
Kyun: \(\tan(\alpha + \beta) = \frac{\tan\alpha + \tan\beta}{1 - \tan\alpha\tan\beta}\), aur \(\tan 60^{\circ} = \sqrt{3}\), \(\tan 45^{\circ} = 1\). Ek doosra raasta bhi hai: step 1 ko step 2 se divide kar dein (\(\tan = \frac{\sin}{\cos}\)); \(2\sqrt{2}\) cancel ho kar wahi jawab aata hai.

Step 4: \(\cot 105^{\circ}\)
\[\cot 105^{\circ} = \dfrac{1}{\tan 105^{\circ}} = \dfrac{1-\sqrt{3}}{1+\sqrt{3}}\]
Kyun: cot, tan ka ulta hai, is liye step 3 wale fraction ko ulat diya: jo upar tha woh neeche, jo neeche tha woh upar.

Step 5: \(\operatorname{cosec} 105^{\circ}\)
\[\operatorname{cosec} 105^{\circ} = \dfrac{1}{\sin 105^{\circ}} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}+1}\]
Kyun: cosec, sin ka ulta hai; step 1 ka fraction ulat diya.

Step 6: \(\sec 105^{\circ}\)
\[\sec 105^{\circ} = \dfrac{1}{\cos 105^{\circ}} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{1-\sqrt{3}}\]
Kyun: sec, cos ka ulta hai; step 2 ka fraction ulat diya.

Tasdeeq:
Pythagorean identity se check karte hain:
\[\sin^{2}105^{\circ} + \cos^{2}105^{\circ}\]
\[= \dfrac{(\sqrt{3}+1)^{2} + (1-\sqrt{3})^{2}}{8}\]
\[= \dfrac{(4+2\sqrt{3}) + (4-2\sqrt{3})}{8} = 1\]
Bilkul 1 aaya. Signs bhi dekh lein: doosre quadrant mein sirf \(\sin\) aur \(\operatorname{cosec}\) positive hote hain; humare \(\cos\), \(\tan\), \(\cot\), \(\sec\) sab negative hain kyun ke un mein \(1 - \sqrt{3}\) hai. Sab theek!

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
Example 6 mein kitab do reciprocal values ghalat chhaapti hai:
1. Kitab ne \(\cot 105^{\circ}\) ka jawab \(\frac{1-\sqrt{3}}{1-\sqrt{3}}\) likha hai, jo to 1 ke barabar hoga! Sahi jawab \(\cot 105^{\circ} = \frac{1-\sqrt{3}}{1+\sqrt{3}} = \sqrt{3} - 2\) hai. Neeche wala sign plus hona chahiye tha.
2. Kitab ne \(\operatorname{cosec} 105^{\circ}\) ka jawab \(\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2\sqrt{2}}\) likha hai, jo asal mein \(\sin 105^{\circ}\) hai, ulta nahin kiya gaya. Sahi jawab \(\operatorname{cosec} 105^{\circ} = \frac{2\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}+1} = \sqrt{6} - \sqrt{2}\) hai.
Upar humne sahi values likhi hain. Exam mein sahi value hi likhiye.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
In jawabon ko rationalize (denominator se root hatana) kar ke chhota bhi kiya ja sakta hai:
\(\sin 105^{\circ} = \frac{\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2}}{4}\), \(\cos 105^{\circ} = \frac{\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{6}}{4}\), \(\tan 105^{\circ} = -(2+\sqrt{3})\), \(\cot 105^{\circ} = \sqrt{3}-2\), \(\operatorname{cosec} 105^{\circ} = \sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2}\), \(\sec 105^{\circ} = -(\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2})\).
Misal ke taur par tan: upar neeche \(1+\sqrt{3}\) se multiply kariye: \(\frac{(1+\sqrt{3})^{2}}{1 - 3} = \frac{4+2\sqrt{3}}{-2} = -(2+\sqrt{3})\). Neeche \((a-b)(a+b) = a^{2}-b^{2}\) ki wajah se root khatam ho gaya. Jab tak sawal simplified jawab na maange, dono shakal qabool hain.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahin: \(\sin 75^{\circ}\) nikaaliye.
\(75^{\circ} = 45^{\circ} + 30^{\circ}\), is liye \(\sin 75^{\circ} = \sin 45^{\circ}\cos 30^{\circ} + \cos 45^{\circ}\sin 30^{\circ} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot\frac{1}{2} = \frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2\sqrt{2}}\).
Dilchasp baat: yeh \(\sin 105^{\circ}\) ke barabar hai! Kyun? Kyun ke \(\sin(180^{\circ} - \theta) = \sin\theta\), aur \(180^{\circ} - 75^{\circ} = 105^{\circ}\). Allied angles ka rule yahan bhi tasdeeq kar raha hai.
Agla example dikhata hai ke kabhi kabhi R.H.S. se shuru karna behtar hota hai, aur \(45^{\circ}\) ka angle kitna kaam ka hai.

blocks.title: Example 7
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(\frac{\cos 11^{\circ} + \sin 11^{\circ}}{\cos 11^{\circ} - \sin 11^{\circ}}\), R.H.S. \(\tan 56^{\circ}\).
To prove: dono barabar hain.
Method: sab se pehle numbers par ghor kariye: \(56^{\circ} - 11^{\circ} = 45^{\circ}\). Yani \(56^{\circ} = 45^{\circ} + 11^{\circ}\). Aur \(\tan 45^{\circ} = 1\) hai, jo formula ko bohat aasan bana deta hai. Is liye R.H.S. se shuru karenge, \(\tan(\alpha + \beta)\) lagayenge, aur phir \(\tan 11^{\circ}\) ko \(\frac{\sin 11^{\circ}}{\cos 11^{\circ}}\) likhenge.

Step 1: R.H.S. ko kholein
\[\text{R.H.S.} = \tan 56^{\circ} = \tan(45^{\circ} + 11^{\circ})\]
\[= \dfrac{\tan 45^{\circ} + \tan 11^{\circ}}{1 - \tan 45^{\circ}\tan 11^{\circ}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1 + \tan 11^{\circ}}{1 - \tan 11^{\circ}}\]
Kyun: \(\tan 45^{\circ} = 1\) rakhne se formula mein sirf ek hi unknown ratio, \(\tan 11^{\circ}\), bacha.

Step 2: Tan ko sin aur cos mein badlein
\[= \dfrac{1 + \frac{\sin 11^{\circ}}{\cos 11^{\circ}}}{1 - \frac{\sin 11^{\circ}}{\cos 11^{\circ}}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\cos 11^{\circ} + \sin 11^{\circ}}{\cos 11^{\circ} - \sin 11^{\circ}} = \text{L.H.S.}\]
Kyun: L.H.S. mein sin aur cos hain, is liye R.H.S. ko bhi usi zubaan mein likhna hai. Upar aur neeche dono ko \(\cos 11^{\circ}\) se multiply kiya to chhote fractions khatam ho gaye (yeh fraction ki value nahin badalta, kyun ke hum asal mein 1 se multiply kar rahe hain).

Tasdeeq:
Calculator se: \(\cos 11^{\circ} \approx 0.9816\), \(\sin 11^{\circ} \approx 0.1908\). L.H.S. \(\approx \frac{1.1724}{0.7908} \approx 1.4826\), aur \(\tan 56^{\circ} \approx 1.4826\). Barabar!

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Yeh pattern yaad rakhiye: \(\frac{\cos x + \sin x}{\cos x - \sin x} = \frac{1 + \tan x}{1 - \tan x} = \tan(45^{\circ} + x)\). Aur ulta: \(\frac{\cos x - \sin x}{\cos x + \sin x} = \tan(45^{\circ} - x)\). Jab bhi sawal mein \(\cos\) aur \(\sin\) ka jor aur farq ek fraction mein dikhe, foran \(45^{\circ}\) zehan mein laiye.
Ab ek bohat ahem qisam ka sawal aata hai: ek ratio aur quadrant diya ho, baqi ratios khud nikaalne hon. Yahan asal imtehan signs ka hai.

blocks.title: Example 8
blocks.problem: If \(\cos\alpha = -\frac{7}{25}\), \(\tan\beta = \frac{12}{5}\), the terminal side of the angle of measure \(\alpha\) is in the II quadrant and that of \(\beta\) is in the III quadrant, find the values of: (i) \(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\) (ii) \(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\). In which quadrant does the terminal side of the angle of measure \((\alpha + \beta)\) lie?
steps:
Given: \(\cos\alpha = -\frac{7}{25}\), \(\alpha\) doosre (II) quadrant mein; \(\tan\beta = \frac{12}{5}\), \(\beta\) teesre (III) quadrant mein.
To find: \(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\), \(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\), aur \(\alpha + \beta\) kis quadrant mein hai.
Method: sum formulas ko chaar cheezein chahiye: \(\sin\alpha\), \(\cos\alpha\), \(\sin\beta\), \(\cos\beta\). Humare paas sirf \(\cos\alpha\) aur \(\tan\beta\) hain. Baqi ko Pythagorean identities se nikalenge, aur har square root ka sign quadrant dekh kar chunenge. Yaad rakhne ka tareeqa 'All Silver Tea Cups': I mein sab positive, II mein sin, III mein tan, IV mein cos.

Step 1: \(\sin\alpha\) nikaalein
\[\sin\alpha = \pm\sqrt{1 - \cos^{2}\alpha}\]
\[= \pm\sqrt{1 - \left(-\dfrac{7}{25}\right)^{2}} = \pm\sqrt{\dfrac{576}{625}}\]
\[= \pm\dfrac{24}{25}\]
\(\alpha\) doosre quadrant mein hai jahan \(\sin\) positive hota hai, is liye:
\[\sin\alpha = \dfrac{24}{25}\]
Kyun: \(\sin^{2}\alpha + \cos^{2}\alpha = 1\) se. \(1 - \frac{49}{625} = \frac{576}{625}\), aur \(576 = 24^{2}\). Square root hamesha do sign deta hai; quadrant faisla karta hai ke kaunsa lena hai.
Dhyan dein: kitab yahan ghalti se minus sign chhaap deti hai (neeche 'Kitab ki ghalti' dekhiye). Sahi value plus hai.

Step 2: \(\sec\beta\) aur \(\cos\beta\) nikaalein
\[\sec\beta = \pm\sqrt{1 + \tan^{2}\beta} = \pm\sqrt{1 + \left(\dfrac{12}{5}\right)^{2}}\]
\[= \pm\dfrac{13}{5}\]
Teesre quadrant mein \(\sec\beta\) negative hai:
\[\sec\beta = -\dfrac{13}{5}, \quad \cos\beta = -\dfrac{5}{13}\]
Kyun: \(\tan\beta\) diya hai, aur jo identity tan ko kisi aur ratio se jorti hai woh \(1 + \tan^{2}\beta = \sec^{2}\beta\) hai. \(1 + \frac{144}{25} = \frac{169}{25}\), aur \(169 = 13^{2}\). Phir cos, sec ka ulta hai. Teesre quadrant mein sirf tan aur cot positive hain, is liye sec aur cos negative.

Step 3: \(\sin\beta\) nikaalein
\[\sin\beta = \pm\sqrt{1 - \cos^{2}\beta} = \pm\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{25}{169}}\]
\[= \pm\sqrt{\dfrac{144}{169}} = \pm\dfrac{12}{13}\]
Teesre quadrant mein \(\sin\beta\) negative: \(\sin\beta = -\frac{12}{13}\).
Kyun: step 1 wali identity. Choti si tasdeeq: \(\frac{\sin\beta}{\cos\beta} = \frac{-12/13}{-5/13} = \frac{12}{5}\), jo diya hua \(\tan\beta\) hai. Matlab dono signs sahi chune.

Step 4: \(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\)
\[\sin(\alpha + \beta) = \sin\alpha\cos\beta + \cos\alpha\sin\beta\]
\[= \dfrac{24}{25}\left(-\dfrac{5}{13}\right) + \left(-\dfrac{7}{25}\right)\left(-\dfrac{12}{13}\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{-120 + 84}{325} = -\dfrac{36}{325}\]
Kyun: sine ka sum formula. \(25 \times 13 = 325\) common denominator. Doosre term mein minus ka minus se guna plus deta hai: \(+\frac{84}{325}\).

Step 5: \(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\)
\[\cos(\alpha + \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta - \sin\alpha\sin\beta\]
\[= \left(-\dfrac{7}{25}\right)\left(-\dfrac{5}{13}\right) - \dfrac{24}{25}\left(-\dfrac{12}{13}\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{35 + 288}{325} = \dfrac{323}{325}\]
Kyun: cosine ka sum formula (beech mein minus). \(-\frac{24}{25}\cdot\left(-\frac{12}{13}\right) = +\frac{288}{325}\): negative cheez ko minus karna use jama karna hai.

Step 6: \(\alpha + \beta\) ka quadrant
\(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\) negative aur \(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\) positive hai, is liye \(\alpha + \beta\) ka terminal arm chauthe (IV) quadrant mein hai.
Kyun: sirf chautha quadrant hi aisa hai jahan cos positive aur sin negative hota hai.

Tasdeeq:
\[\left(-\dfrac{36}{325}\right)^{2} + \left(\dfrac{323}{325}\right)^{2} = \dfrac{1296 + 104329}{105625} = 1\]
Jawab \(\sin^{2} + \cos^{2} = 1\) ko poora karte hain, is liye hisaab durust hai.
blocks.answer: (i) \(\sin(\alpha + \beta) = -\frac{36}{325}\) (ii) \(\cos(\alpha + \beta) = \frac{323}{325}\); \(\alpha + \beta\) ka terminal side chauthe (IV) quadrant mein hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Example 8 mein kitab khud likhti hai ke doosre quadrant mein \(\sin\alpha\) positive hai, aur phir agli line mein 'So \(\sin\alpha = -\frac{24}{25}\)' chhaap deti hai. Sahi value \(\sin\alpha = +\frac{24}{25}\) hai. Kitab ka aage ka hisaab \(\frac{24}{25}\) hi use karta hai, is liye final jawab sahi hain; sirf woh ek line ghalat chhapi hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Agar Example 8 mein \(\alpha\) doosre ki bajaye teesre quadrant mein hota (aur \(\cos\alpha = -\frac{7}{25}\) hi rehta), to \(\sin\alpha\) kya hota? Jawab: \(-\frac{24}{25}\), kyun ke teesre quadrant mein sin negative hai. Dekha, quadrant badla to sirf sign badla, number wahi raha.
Ab triangle ke angles wala example. Yahan raaz ek hi hai: triangle ke teeno angles ka jor \(180^{\circ}\) hota hai.

blocks.title: Example 9
blocks.problem: If \(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\) are the angles of \(\Delta ABC\), prove that: (i) \(\tan\alpha + \tan\beta + \tan\gamma = \tan\alpha\tan\beta\tan\gamma\) (ii) \(\tan\frac{\alpha}{2}\tan\frac{\beta}{2} + \tan\frac{\beta}{2}\tan\frac{\gamma}{2} + \tan\frac{\gamma}{2}\tan\frac{\alpha}{2} = 1\)
steps:
Given: \(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\) triangle \(ABC\) ke angles hain, is liye \(\alpha + \beta + \gamma = 180^{\circ}\).
To prove: tangent wale do natije (i) aur (ii).
Method: do angles ka jor teesre angle ki shakal mein likhenge, dono taraf tan lenge, \(\tan(\alpha + \beta)\) aur allied angles ke rule se kholenge, phir cross-multiply kar ke terms ek taraf karenge.

Step 1 (i): \(\alpha + \beta\) ko \(\gamma\) se likhein
\[\alpha + \beta + \gamma = 180^{\circ}\]
\[\alpha + \beta = 180^{\circ} - \gamma\]
\[\tan(\alpha + \beta) = \tan(180^{\circ} - \gamma)\]
Kyun: barabar angles ke tan bhi barabar. Is tarah teeno angles ek equation mein aa gaye.

Step 2 (i): Dono sides kholein
\[\dfrac{\tan\alpha + \tan\beta}{1 - \tan\alpha\tan\beta} = -\tan\gamma\]
Kyun: left side par sum formula. Right side par allied angle ka rule: \(180^{\circ}\), \(90^{\circ}\) ka even multiple hai, is liye tan, tan hi rehta hai; aur \(180^{\circ} - \gamma\) doosre quadrant mein hai jahan tan negative hai. Is liye \(\tan(180^{\circ} - \gamma) = -\tan\gamma\).

Step 3 (i): Cross-multiply aur tarteeb dein
\[\tan\alpha + \tan\beta = -\tan\gamma + \tan\alpha\tan\beta\tan\gamma\]
\[\tan\alpha + \tan\beta + \tan\gamma = \tan\alpha\tan\beta\tan\gamma\]
Kyun: dono sides ko \(1 - \tan\alpha\tan\beta\) se multiply kiya: \(-\tan\gamma(1 - \tan\alpha\tan\beta) = -\tan\gamma + \tan\alpha\tan\beta\tan\gamma\). Phir \(\tan\gamma\) ko left side par le aaye (sign badal kar).

Step 4 (ii): Half angles banayein
\[\dfrac{\alpha}{2} + \dfrac{\beta}{2} + \dfrac{\gamma}{2} = 90^{\circ}\]
\[\dfrac{\alpha}{2} + \dfrac{\beta}{2} = 90^{\circ} - \dfrac{\gamma}{2}\]
\[\tan\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{2} + \dfrac{\beta}{2}\right) = \tan\left(90^{\circ} - \dfrac{\gamma}{2}\right)\]
Kyun: natija (ii) mein aadhe angles hain, is liye poori equation ko 2 se divide kar diya. Baqi tareeqa bilkul (i) jaisa hai.

Step 5 (ii): Dono sides kholein
\[\dfrac{\tan\frac{\alpha}{2} + \tan\frac{\beta}{2}}{1 - \tan\frac{\alpha}{2}\tan\frac{\beta}{2}} = \cot\dfrac{\gamma}{2}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{\tan\frac{\gamma}{2}}\]
Kyun: \(\tan(90^{\circ} - \theta) = \cot\theta\). Yahan \(90^{\circ}\) odd multiple hai, is liye tan apne co-ratio cot mein badal jata hai; pehla quadrant hai to sign positive.

Step 6 (ii): Cross-multiply aur tarteeb dein
\[\tan\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\tan\dfrac{\gamma}{2} + \tan\dfrac{\beta}{2}\tan\dfrac{\gamma}{2}\]
\[= 1 - \tan\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\tan\dfrac{\beta}{2}\]
Aakhri term ko left par le aayein:
\[\tan\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\tan\dfrac{\beta}{2} + \tan\dfrac{\beta}{2}\tan\dfrac{\gamma}{2}\]
\[+ \tan\dfrac{\gamma}{2}\tan\dfrac{\alpha}{2} = 1\]
Kyun: left ke numerator ko \(\tan\frac{\gamma}{2}\) se aur right ke 1 ko denominator se multiply kiya (cross-multiplication). Phir saare products ek taraf jama kiye, taa ke natija kitab wali shakal mein aa jaye.

Tasdeeq:
Equilateral triangle lijiye, \(\alpha = \beta = \gamma = 60^{\circ}\). (i): L.H.S. \(= 3\sqrt{3}\), R.H.S. \(= (\sqrt{3})^{3} = 3\sqrt{3}\). Barabar. (ii): \(\tan 30^{\circ} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\), har product \(\frac{1}{3}\), teen products ka jor \(1\). Bilkul sahi!

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Natija (i) sirf us triangle ke liye hai jis mein koi angle \(90^{\circ}\) na ho, kyun ke \(\tan 90^{\circ}\) defined hi nahin. Natija (ii) har triangle ke liye sahi hai, kyun ke har aadha angle \(90^{\circ}\) se chhota hota hai, is liye uska tan hamesha mojood hai.
Aakhri example ek naya hunar sikhata hai: \(\sin\) aur \(\cos\) ke jor ko ek hi sine mein badalna. Physics mein waves aur alternating current mein yahi kaam aata hai.

blocks.title: Example 10
blocks.problem: Express \(3\sin\theta + 4\cos\theta\) in the form \(r\sin(\theta + \phi)\), where the terminal side of the angle of measure \(\phi\) is in quadrant I.
steps:
Given: expression \(3\sin\theta + 4\cos\theta\).
To find: \(r\) aur \(\phi\) (pehle quadrant mein) aise ke \(3\sin\theta + 4\cos\theta = r\sin(\theta + \phi)\).
Method: pehle dekhiye ke \(r\sin(\theta + \phi)\) khulta kaise hai: \(r\cos\phi\sin\theta + r\sin\phi\cos\theta\). Ab dono taraf \(\sin\theta\) ke coefficients aur \(\cos\theta\) ke coefficients barabar kar denge: \(r\cos\phi = 3\), \(r\sin\phi = 4\). Phir in do equations se \(r\) aur \(\phi\) nikalenge.

Step 1: Do equations likhein
\[3 = r\cos\phi \quad \text{(i)}\]
\[4 = r\sin\phi \quad \text{(ii)}\]
Kyun: \(\sin\theta\) ka coefficient \(r\cos\phi\) hai aur \(\cos\theta\) ka coefficient \(r\sin\phi\). Dhyan dein, 3 cos ke saath aur 4 sin ke saath jata hai, ulta nahin.

Step 2: (i) aur (ii) ko square kar ke jama karein, \(r\) nikaalein
\[3^{2} + 4^{2} = r^{2}\cos^{2}\phi + r^{2}\sin^{2}\phi\]
\[9 + 16 = r^{2}(\cos^{2}\phi + \sin^{2}\phi)\]
\[25 = r^{2} \Rightarrow r = 5\]
Kyun: square kar ke jama karne se \(\phi\) gayab ho jata hai, kyun ke \(\cos^{2}\phi + \sin^{2}\phi = 1\). \(r\) ek lambai jaisi cheez hai, is liye positive value \(5\) lete hain.

Step 3: (ii) ko (i) se divide karein, \(\phi\) nikaalein
\[\dfrac{4}{3} = \dfrac{r\sin\phi}{r\cos\phi} = \tan\phi\]
\[\phi = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{4}{3}\]
Kyun: divide karne se \(r\) cancel ho jata hai aur sirf \(\tan\phi\) bachta hai. \(\sin\phi\) aur \(\cos\phi\) dono positive hain, is liye \(\phi\) pehle quadrant mein hai, jaisa sawal ne maanga (taqreeban \(53.13^{\circ}\)).

Step 4: Expression ko maangi gayi shakal mein likhein
\[3\sin\theta + 4\cos\theta = r\cos\phi\sin\theta + r\sin\phi\cos\theta\]
\[= r(\sin\theta\cos\phi + \cos\theta\sin\phi)\]
\[= r\sin(\theta + \phi)\]
Kyun: 3 aur 4 ki jagah (i) aur (ii) rakhe, \(r\) common nikala, aur bracket mein sine ka sum formula pehchaan liya.

Tasdeeq:
\(\cos\phi = \frac{3}{5}\), \(\sin\phi = \frac{4}{5}\) (yeh 3-4-5 wala mashhoor right triangle hai). \(5\sin(\theta + \phi) = 5\left(\frac{3}{5}\sin\theta + \frac{4}{5}\cos\theta\right) = 3\sin\theta + 4\cos\theta\). Wapas asal expression mil gaya.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Aam rule: \(a\sin\theta + b\cos\theta = r\sin(\theta + \phi)\), jahan \(r = \sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}}\) aur \(\tan\phi = \frac{b}{a}\).
Agar beech mein minus ho: \(a\sin\theta - b\cos\theta = r\sin(\theta - \phi)\), wahi \(r\) aur wahi \(\phi\) (\(r\sin(\theta - \phi)\) khol kar khud dekhiye kyun). Exercise 10.2 ke sawal 15 mein yahi kaam aayega.
Ek faida aur: \(\sin(\theta + \phi)\) hamesha \(-1\) aur \(1\) ke darmiyan rehta hai, is liye \(3\sin\theta + 4\cos\theta\) ki sab se bari value 5 aur sab se chhoti \(-5\) hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahin: \(\sin\theta + \sqrt{3}\cos\theta\) ko \(r\sin(\theta + \phi)\) mein likhiye.
\(a = 1\), \(b = \sqrt{3}\). \(r = \sqrt{1 + 3} = 2\). \(\tan\phi = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{1} = \sqrt{3}\), is liye \(\phi = 60^{\circ}\).
Jawab: \(\sin\theta + \sqrt{3}\cos\theta = 2\sin(\theta + 60^{\circ})\). Tasdeeq: \(2(\sin\theta\cdot\frac{1}{2} + \cos\theta\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) = \sin\theta + \sqrt{3}\cos\theta\). Sahi!

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Jo angle table mein na ho (\(105^{\circ}\), \(15^{\circ}\), \(75^{\circ}\)), use \(30^{\circ}, 45^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}\) ke jor ya farq se likhiye.
2. \(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\sin(\alpha - \beta) = \sin^{2}\alpha - \sin^{2}\beta = \cos^{2}\beta - \cos^{2}\alpha\).
3. \(\frac{1 + \tan x}{1 - \tan x} = \tan(45^{\circ} + x)\).
4. Ek ratio aur quadrant diya ho to baqi ratios \(\sin^{2} + \cos^{2} = 1\) ya \(1 + \tan^{2} = \sec^{2}\) se nikaaliye, aur har sign quadrant se chuniye.
5. Triangle mein \(\alpha + \beta + \gamma = 180^{\circ}\): ek angle ko baqi do se likhiye aur tan lijiye.
6. \(a\sin\theta + b\cos\theta = r\sin(\theta + \phi)\), \(r = \sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}\), \(\tan\phi = \frac{b}{a}\).
7. Har jawab ko kisi aasan tareeqe (Pythagorean identity, calculator, ya aasan angle) se check zaroor kijiye.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(\sin(60^{\circ} + 45^{\circ}) = \sin 60^{\circ} + \sin 45^{\circ}\) likh dena. Yeh bilkul ghalat hai; sine jor par taqseem nahin hota. Hamesha formula lagaiye.
2. \(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\) mein beech ka sign plus likh dena. Yaad rakhiye: cos mein sign ulat jata hai.
3. Square root lete waqt \(\pm\) ko chhor dena, ya quadrant dekhe baghair plus le lena. Pehle quadrant likhiye, phir sign chuniye.
4. \(\cot\), \(\operatorname{cosec}\), \(\sec\) nikalte waqt fraction ka sirf aadha hissa ulatna. Poora fraction ulatiye; kitab ne bhi yahin ghalti ki hai.
5. \(a\sin\theta + b\cos\theta\) mein \(\tan\phi = \frac{a}{b}\) le lena. Sahi \(\tan\phi = \frac{b}{a}\) hai (cos wale coefficient upar).
